newsitem.title: UK: Allders wants to abandon share consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Allders wants to abandon share consolidation.

text.p: UK department store and retail outlet operator Allders Plc said on Wednesday that shareholders should vote against resolutions at Thursday's extraordinary meeting relating to a share capital consolidation.

"If the resolutions are not passed at tomorrow's meeting, the board of Allders intends to propose the payment of a special dividend of 46p per share, equal to a total payment of approximately 50 million stg," it said.
The government on Tuesday announced amendments to laws governing the availability of tax credits on company distributions, which prompted Allders' statement.
The original share consolidation had been planned to accompany the 50 million stg special dividend.

But the group said while details of the proposed legal changes had still to emerge, the Chancellor had indicated if a special dividend was paid which was not linked to a share capital consolidation, UK resident shareholders that do not have to pay tax should continue to get payment of tax credit.
Allders said it had wanted to consolidate its share capital to allow consistent calculation of earnings per share and to maintain the position of over 750 employee share option holders.

"The board of Allders regrets that the Chancellor's proposed amendments, the principal aim of which is to reduce costs for the exchequer, should prevent Allders from achieving its objectives in this way," it said in a statement.
It said it therefore intended to propose that the special dividend be paid as previously indicated but without the associated share capital consolidation.

Allders said it intended to "put alternative arrangements in place as soon as possible to compensate employee option holders for the loss of value arising from payment of the special dividend, in the absence of the share capital consolidation".
